chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj while he did not know this matter (of Wilayah), then God granted him knowledge of it and devotion to it; is the Hajj of Islam sufficient for him, or has he fulfilled his obligation? He said: 'He has fulfilled his obligation, and if he performed it again, it would be more beloved to me.'

He said: And I asked him about a man who was from one of these categories of the people of the Qibla, a devout Nasibi (one who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt), then God granted him knowledge and he recognized this matter; does he fulfill the Hajj of Islam? He said: 'He fulfills it, it is more beloved to me.'

He said: 'Every deed he performed while in the state of his opposition and misguidance, then God granted him knowledge and he recognized the Wilayah, he is rewarded for it, except for Zakat, for he must repeat it, because he placed it in its non-appropriate places, because it belongs to the people of Wilayah. As for Salat, Hajj, and Sawm, he does not need to repeat them.'

In it (24) And that which Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Hamdani wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I performed Hajj while I was opposing (the Ahl al-Bayt), and I was a Sururi (a specific sect), so I entered performing Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj). He (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Repeat your Hajj.'

So this narration is also based on recommendation (istihbab) rather than obligation (fard), and that which indicates this is what we preceded with from the narration of Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he said 'He has fulfilled his obligation, and if he performed it again, it would be more beloved to me.'

And it is also indicated by what was narrated: (25) Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah said: I wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj and did not know or recognize this matter, then God granted him knowledge of it and devotion to it; is the Hajj of Islam upon him, or has he fulfilled the obligation of God? He said: 'He has fulfilled the obligation of God, and Hajj is more beloved to me.'

And about a man who is from one of these categories of the people of the Qibla, a devout Nasibi, then God granted him knowledge and he recognized this matter; is the Hajj of Islam fulfilled for him, or is it upon him to perform Hajj next year? He said: 'He performs Hajj, it is more beloved to me.'
And we have previously mentioned that the existence of wealth in the form of provisions and mounts is among the conditions for the obligation of Hajj, and this does not contradict what was narrated.

key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: Alms-tax, distinguished here as requiring repetition if given to the wrong recipients
key_terms.الْوِلَايَةُ: Divine guardianship/authority, specifically of the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.نَاصِبٍ: One who opposes or is hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: Does a person's Hajj count if they were not aware of the Ahl al-Bayt's Wilayah at the time, and do they need to repeat it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia jurisprudential stance on the validity of Hajj for those lacking full knowledge of *Wilayah*, establishing that while their initial pilgrimage fulfills the obligatory duty (*fard*), performing it again is preferred (*ahabb ilayy*). It further distinguishes between ritual acts like prayer and fasting, which remain valid despite prior ignorance, and Zakat, which must be repeated because it was distributed to those not entitled to it due to their lack of *Wilayah* recognition. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *Wilayah* as a core component of religious validity, influencing both the acceptance of past deeds and the distribution of wealth.
